meta.title: 21 Tips I Wish I Knew Before Visiting Vietnam
meta.description:
☕️ Every Tuesday, I share a travel tip you’ll actually use — like advice from a friend who travels nonstop -- https://bit.ly/TheTuesdayTravelTip

These 21 tips to know before visiting Vietnam are what I wish I knew before my trip to Vietnam. Hopefully these travel tips will help you from making some of the mistakes I made when traveling through Vietnam!

The eSIM I use to keep my phone connected  -- https://airalo.pxf.io/CamdenDavid -- You can get 15% off by using code: CAMDEN15

DISCLAIMER: I only express my opinion based on my experience. Your experience may be different. Links above may include affiliate commission or referrals. I'm part of an affiliate network and I receive compensation from partnering websites. This video is accurate as of the posting date but may not be accurate in the future.

comments.author: @NguyenDuyKhanh02
comments.text:
Là một người Việt Nam tôi có thể khẳng định rằng những món ăn đường phố đều ngon hơn nhà hàng. Đây không phải điều vô lý sau khi bạn biết rằng những phố phường và khu chợ là nơi hình thành nên văn hoá, truyền thống. Người Việt xưa thường đi chợ vào sáng sớm để chuẩn bị bữa ăn, những người bán hàng cũng sẽ dậy từ rất sớm để chuẩn bị cho gian hàng vì vậy nên buổi sáng sẽ rất tấp lập. Sau khi đi về từ khu chợ ,thông thường họ sẽ tập thể dục lúc 6 giờ sáng và 6 chiều, bạn sẽ thấy khung cảnh rất nhiều ở công viên và bãi biển. Không khí chợ sáng sớm và không khí đón bình minh rất tuyệt vời, tôi nghĩ bạn nên thử nó. Một điều khác tôi muốn nói là khi chọn quán ăn, thay vì chọn chỗ du lịch và có đông người du lịch thì hãy tìm chỗ có nhiều người địa phương tìm đến, nó rẻ hơn và ngon hơn. Nhưng đừng chọn quán ăn có giá thấp hơn so với các quán ăn xung quanh, nếu tốt nhất thì hãy hỏi những người địa phương

Một điều thú vị nữa là "cà phê trứng" được tạo ra trong khoảng thời gian thiếu thốn nguyên liệu, họ cho lòng đỏ trứng vào cà phê để thay cho sữa đặc khan hiếm

comments.text:
One of the best meal I ever had was in a dirty Central Highlands city called Kontum.  At about 5am, I pulled my motorbike over and bought a sandwich from an early-opening stand.  The vender’s English was as negligible as my Vietnamese so I just pointed to one of the sandwiches already made.
It was really delicious: creamy and rich and oddly sweet — and tantalizingly familiar.  After a few bites, I cracked it open: the filling was... granulated sugar and butter.
Now, I cannot recommend this dish as an actual food, but at that moment, jet-lagged, sleep-deprived, isolated, my body needed exactly that.

If a place called [I'm making this up] Joe's Pizza gets lots of good reviews in Google or other apps, there are unscrupulous people who open their own restaurant with THE SAME NAME in a nearby location, as a means of stealing away those people who are looking for the original restaurant.

comments.author: @Specialone888-c5v
comments.text: Don’t believe all of these fake social media influencers and lying YouTube posts who make Vietnam look like the hot new paradise on earth because it isn’t.  Just went to visit Vietnam and check it out and it’s a 6 out of 10.  Thailand is much better 9/10 for many reasons like much better infrastructure, the politeness of the local Thai people.  In Vietnam the vibe is more aggressive & rude like back in America and the language barrier is worse than you think so you can’t communicate with the people.  Plus the big elephant sitting in the living room is the stigma of the horrible Vietnam war dead ghosts still hangs where 58,000 Americans died and 3 million Vietnamese died gives it a weird paranormal feeling.  Reminded me of the killing fields of Cambodia with pol pot who killed 3 million of his own people or visiting world war 2 battlefields in Europe where millions were murdered with the same weird ghost paranormal feelings.  In Vietnam it was a constant surreal experience & feeling to think that my uncle fought only 49 miles from our beach front resort in Da Nang in one of the bloodiest battles of the Vietnam war where thousand perished in bloody door to door combat.  I couldn’t stop thinking about it and remembering his stories of almost being killed by a booby trap bomb toy bear he picked up and exploded in his face placed by the enemy.
